collection.description: A villager and another villager have been hoping for a baby for a long time.

ask.text:
(subject) and (friend) have been hoping for a baby for a long time. They don't talk about it much, but everyone knows, the way everyone in a small village knows everything.
(healer), the oldest healer, finds them one evening and presses two smooth river stones into their hands, warm from (healer.his/her) pocket. "My grandmother gave these to me," (healer.he/she) says. "Put them under your sleeping mat, and drink the leaf tea I'll leave you. It might do nothing. But it might not." Then (healer.he/she) goes away before they can thank (healer.him/her).
They look at each other. Should they try the stones and the tea, or just let things happen in their own time?

choices.label: Try the Stones and the Tea
Let Things Happen in Their Own Time

c1o1.text: A few weeks later, (subject) can't stand the smell of fish, and then can't stop eating mangoes, and then (healer) comes round with a knowing smile. A baby is expected. (friend) runs round the whole village telling everybody, including people who already know, including the pigs. The stones go back to (healer), who puts them in (healer.his/her) pocket and says, "Well. It might not have been the stones."

c1o2.text: A baby is expected. Then, as the weeks go by, (healer) listens to (subject)'s belly for a long time, and frowns, and listens again, and starts counting on (healer.his/her) fingers. "{#babies:One, just the one, i was sure there were more|Two, you'll want a bigger sleeping mat|Three, you'll want a much bigger sleeping mat}," (healer.he/she) says at last. (friend) has to sit down. The village starts building {#babies:a cradle|two cradles|three cradles}.

c1.text: The tea tastes of grass and something sweet. The stones go under the mat. (subject) and (friend) lie awake for a long time that night, holding hands, feeling a little silly and a little hopeful...

c2o1.text: They stop counting the days. They go fishing together, and build a new shelf, and argue cheerfully about where to put it. And one morning, a few months later, (subject) wakes up feeling sick as a dog and knows, before (healer) even says it. A baby is expected. "No stones," (friend) tells everyone proudly. "No tea. Just us."

c2o2.text: No baby comes that season, or the next. Instead, (subject) and (friend) somehow become the couple every child in the village runs to: for a story, for a scraped knee, for a place to hide from chores. Their hut is never quiet. "We'll see," (subject) says, when anyone asks, and means it. Their life is already full.

c2.text: They thank (healer) the next day, and give the stones back. "We'd like to just see what happens," (subject) says. (healer) nods as if (healer.he/she) expected nothing else...
